cover.title: Docker Complete Handbook
cover.subtitle: From Basics to Advanced
cover.tagline: Package once, run the same on any host
pills: 1. What Docker is and why it runs anywhere

items: ==Namespaces== isolate what a process **sees**
==cgroups== limit what it can **use**: CPU, memory, I/O
Container = process with both applied

blocks.note: shared kernel: one exploit hits all

items: Mistake: a container is as strong a wall as a VM
==One host kernel==: a **kernel exploit** hits every container
Run untrusted code in a VM instead

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Walk CLI to runc: who calls whom?
Namespaces do what cgroups do not?
Why is a VM a stronger boundary?
An image is a ==read-only== stack of layers
A container adds one thin **writable** layer on top
Writes use copy-on-write: file copied up, then changed
Docker's storage driver for this is `overlay2`

blocks.title: 5. Mistake: data in the writable layer
items: Database files written inside the container
`docker rm` deletes that layer with its data
Mount a volume at the data path instead

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why is a container's writable layer ephemeral?
What happens in the 10 seconds after docker stop?
When would you choose docker kill over docker stop?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Layers stay read-only; stop is graceful, kill is instant, rm erases the writable layer.

items: Each `RUN`/`COPY` = one ==layer==; a changed layer **invalidates** all after it
`AS build` stage holds compilers and dev deps
==COPY --from=build== takes only output; tools never ship, image stays slim
Shell form wraps `sh -c`, not ==PID 1==: **SIGTERM** ignored, stop waits 10s
`COPY . .` before `npm ci` busts cache every build
No `.dockerignore` (`node_modules`, `.git`, `.env`): secrets in image, bigger context

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why copy package.json before source?
How does multi-stage shrink an image?
CMD vs ENTRYPOINT: `docker run` args?
Why exec form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT?
{icon:database} ==Named volume==: created and managed by Docker
{icon:laptop} ==Bind mount==: a host path mapped into the container
{icon:zap} ==tmpfs==: memory only, gone when the container stops
Data lives under `/var/lib/docker/volumes`, outside the container
Volumes ==survive== `docker rm` of the container
Several containers can mount the **same** volume

blocks.note: source form decides the mount type

blocks.title: REMEMBER:
blocks.text: A name without a slash is a volume; a leading / or ./ makes it a bind mount.

blocks.title: TIP:
blocks.text: Prefer --mount for bind mounts: it errors on a missing host path, while -v silently creates it.

blocks.note: docker rm keeps pgdata; prune deletes it

items: `docker volume prune` deletes every unused volume, no warning
`compose down -v` silently removes the project's volumes
Data written to a **tmpfs** mount vanishes on stop
Bind mounting a wrong path hides the image's files
Volume for data, bind mount for source code
tmpfs for secrets and scratch space
Back up before any prune or down -v

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Volume vs bind mount: when do you pick each?
Does docker rm delete a named volume?
What does compose down -v remove?
Where does a tmpfs mount keep its data?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Keep data in named volumes, and never prune or down -v blindly.

items: `-p 8080:80` is host port : container port
Client `host:8080` → ==iptables NAT== (DNAT) → container `:80`
Unpublished ports stay reachable only inside the network

blocks.note: names resolve only on user-defined networks

items: Service bound to `127.0.0.1` inside the container
Loopback is the container's own, so ==-p== traffic never arrives
Bind `0.0.0.0` instead, then publish the port

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why no names on the default bridge?
What does `-p 8080:80` do underneath?
Why is a 127.0.0.1 bind unreachable?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Use a user-defined bridge for name DNS, publish ports with -p, and bind 0.0.0.0.

items: `compose.yaml` declares ==services==, networks, volumes; replaces long `docker run` commands
`docker compose up` builds, creates, starts the stack; `down` removes containers and networks
==One default network== per project; services reach each other by **service name**, no IPs or `--link`; ports publish only for the host

blocks.title: TIP:
blocks.text: Run docker compose config to validate the file and print the merged result of all -f files.

items: Mistake: Compose as ==production orchestration==
It runs on a **single host** only; no self-healing if the host dies
Need multiple hosts? Use Swarm or Kubernetes

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: What does `docker compose up` do?
How do services find each other by name?
started vs healthy in depends_on?
Why is Compose not production orchestration?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Compose describes a stack on one host; health conditions, not order, make it ready.

items: A ==registry== stores images, organised by repository and tag
{icon:docker} **Docker Hub**: the default public registry
{icon:github} **GHCR**, {icon:ecr} **ECR**: hosted by GitHub and AWS
Self-host a private one with `registry:2`
`:latest` is just a default tag, ==not newest==
Two builds tagged latest make rollbacks **ambiguous**
Rolling back to `:latest` can re-pull the bad image

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why is a tag mutable but a digest not?
Why avoid :latest in production?
What happens between docker login and docker push?
Default user is {red:root} (UID 0); escape means **root** on host
Fix: `RUN adduser -D app`, `USER app`
`--cap-drop ALL`, add back only needed; `no-new-privileges` blocks setuid
Scan: `trivy image app:1.0`, `docker scout cves app:1.0`
`ENV API_KEY=abc` stores secret in image metadata
Deleted file stays in history: `docker history --no-trunc app`
Fix: `RUN --mount=type=secret`, `docker build --secret`; runtime Docker secrets or vault
`USER` set, so the process never runs as root
Capabilities dropped, root filesystem `--read-only`
Base image slim and scanned before every release
Secrets injected at runtime, never baked into layers

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Why is root in a container dangerous?
What do --cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges do?
How to pass a build-time secret safely?
Why distroless over a full OS base?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Run non-root, drop capabilities, ship minimal scanned images, never bake secrets into layers.

rows.label: What it is:
rows.text: A fixed routine to find why a container fails.

rows.label: Start with:
rows.text: Status, logs, then config, before any guesswork.

items: `docker ps -a` lists exited containers, with status
`docker logs -f --tail 100 c` follows the last 100 lines
`docker inspect c`: config, mounts, env; read `State.ExitCode`, `State.OOMKilled`
`docker exec -it c sh` starts a second process in the same namespaces
Exits at start? exec has nothing to attach to; `docker run --entrypoint sh -it img` replaces the crashing command
Main process in background, so container exits at once
`nginx` without `-g 'daemon off;'` exits; run app in foreground as PID 1
Guessing a cause before reading `docker logs`

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Check ps, logs, inspect, then exec; the exit code names the cause. Q: Exit 137? Q: Debug a start crash? Q: Why exit immediately?

items: `--restart unless-stopped` revives crashes, honours manual stops
`HEALTHCHECK` marks ==healthy== or unhealthy, not just running
`--memory`, `--cpus` cap one container; ==log rotation== caps json-file logs
**Scheduling**: node with free CPU, memory
**Scaling**: N replicas, one command
**Rolling updates**: gradual, no downtime
**Self-healing**: restart on any healthy host
Unbounded json-file logs ==fill the disk==
No `--memory`: one leak means **OOM** kill
Restart policy but no HEALTHCHECK

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: Which flags make a container production-ready?
What does an orchestrator add over Docker alone?
Swarm or Kubernetes: how to choose?

blocks.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS:
blocks.text: Set restarts, health, limits, log rotation, then orchestrate; Swarm is simple, Kubernetes is powerful.

rows: drop stopped containers, dangling images; `--volumes` deletes **unused volumes**
COPY copies; ADD untars, fetches URLs
shares host kernel, MBs; VM guest OS, GBs

caption.text:
Everything you need before your Docker interview, in one handwritten carousel. 🐳

From how the engine works under the hood to shipping containers in production, this series walks through Docker start to finish and ends with a command cheat sheet and interview questions you can revise the night before.

Topics covered:
✅ Docker Complete Handbook
✅ Docker Architecture and Internals
✅ Images and Containers Lifecycle
✅ Dockerfile and Build Optimization
✅ Volumes and Storage
✅ Docker Networking
✅ Docker Compose for Multi-Container Apps
✅ Registries and Image Tagging
✅ Docker Security Best Practices
✅ Debugging and Troubleshooting Containers
✅ Production and Orchestration
✅ Docker Cheatsheet and Interview Questions

Who it's for: students, developers, and DevOps beginners who want to learn Docker properly, and anyone preparing for backend, DevOps, or cloud interviews.
